title: Operational Risk
description: Run pyvar's 44 operational-risk functions on the live pyvar.com API: Basel SMA capital, loss distribution approach (LDA/AMA) and OpVaR, RCSA scoring, KRI breach detection, scenario analysis, BEICF and cyber, model, IT and vendor risk. Use when the user wants operational-risk capital or indicator results computed rather than only explained. Needs a free pyvar API key; the skill explains how to get one.
tagline: Operational-risk calculations: SMA and LDA capital, loss data, RCSA, key risk indicators, scenario analysis and governance reporting. Pick the function in **Functions** below; the **Worked examples** show the request shape.

examples.title: Basel SMA capital for a mid-sized bank
examples.intro: The Business Indicator drives the Business Indicator Component; with a loss component the Internal Loss Multiplier adjusts it. Any one currency unit.

examples.title: KRI status, higher-is-worse and lower-is-worse
examples.intro: The same call classifies indicators where a rising value is bad (failed trades) and where a falling value is bad (staff coverage). Direction decides which side of the thresholds is worse.

groups.title: Capital Models — LDA (`engine/oprisk_lda.py`)
groups.intro:
**Regulatory status**: `advanced_measurement_approach_ama` and the LDA/OpVaR
pipeline below are **not** valid for Basel III/IV regulatory capital. The
Standardised Measurement Approach (next section) replaced the AMA as the
sole approach permitted for internationally active banks from 1 January
2022 (BCBS d424, "Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms", Dec 2017).
The module's own docstring says this explicitly: AMA is "retired under
Basel III/IV ... retained here for economic-capital, internal scenario
analysis, and jurisdictions still on earlier timelines only." Use
`basel_standardised_measurement_sma` for the actual regulatory number.
`advanced_measurement_approach_ama`'s `expected_loss_covered` flag
implements the EL/UL choice in Basel II §669(b): if a bank can demonstrate
expected loss is already captured in provisioning/pricing, capital is
unexpected-loss-only (OpVaR − EL); otherwise capital is the full OpVaR.

`frequency_distribution_fitting` is **Poisson-only** (lambda = sample
mean); the `dispersion` (var/mean) it returns is diagnostic only — a value
far from 1 flags over/under-dispersion relative to Poisson, but no
negative-binomial or other alternative frequency fit is implemented.
`severity_distribution_fitting` is **lognormal-only** and raises
`ValueError` for any other `distribution` argument — there is no Weibull,
Gamma, or EVT/generalised-Pareto alternative for the loss tail.

groups.title: Capital Models — SMA & Economic Capital (`engine/oprisk_capital.py`)
groups.intro:
`insurance_offset_calculation`'s 20%-of-capital cap and haircut language
reflect the old **AMA** framework, where insurance mitigation was capped at
20% of the AMA capital charge. The **SMA** that has actually replaced AMA
for regulatory capital does not recognise insurance mitigation at all — a
widely noted gap in the SMA design. So this function (and the
`oprisk_economic_capital` mitigant it feeds) is only meaningful for
internal/economic capital; it has no bearing on the regulatory figure
produced by `basel_standardised_measurement_sma`.

groups.title: Emerging Risk Categories (`engine/oprisk_governance.py`)
groups.intro:
These six are self-authored composite scores (weighted indices / caps
chosen in this codebase) — none of them cite, or claim to implement, a
specific Basel/BCBS formula, unlike the Capital Models and Loss Data
sections above. `model_risk_assessment` and `cyber_risk_loss_estimation`
name the frameworks they take their *shape* from (SR 11-7 / PRA SS1/23-style
materiality x complexity tiering; a FAIR-style single-loss-expectancy
estimate) but the specific weights and thresholds are pyvar's own, not
values prescribed by those frameworks.

notes.monte_carlo_oprisk_capital: OpVaR quantile + ES; default confidence 0.999 (Basel AMA 99.9%/1yr), enforced in [0.90, 0.9999]
notes.operational_var_opvar: quantile reader over a supplied annual-loss sample
notes.advanced_measurement_approach_ama: retired for Basel III/IV regulatory capital (superseded by SMA); economic-capital use only
notes.basel_standardised_measurement_sma: the only function here valid for Basel III/IV regulatory capital. BIC piecewise on Business Indicator buckets EUR [0,1bn]/(1bn,30bn]/(>30bn] at 12%/15%/18% marginal coefficients; ILM = ln(e-1+(LC/BIC)^0.8), LC = 15x average annual losses, bucket-1 banks may fix ILM=1 (BCBS d424, 2017)
notes.oprisk_capital_allocation: pro-rata by standalone risk, sums to total
notes.diversification_benefit_oprisk: sqrt(k @ corr @ k) under a single uniform pairwise correlation; an economic-capital technique, not a Basel-prescribed one
notes.insurance_offset_calculation: AMA-era 20% cap language; not recognised under the SMA that replaced AMA for regulatory capital
notes.tail_risk_scenario_oprisk: tail ES scaled by a severity multiplier
notes.loss_data_collection_framework: filters events at/above a reporting threshold
notes.loss_event_classification_basel: validates against the 7 Basel II Level-1 event-type categories (BCBS 128, Annex 9)
notes.rcsa_risk_identification: validates/summarises a risk register by Basel category
notes.rcsa_inherent_risk_scoring: likelihood x impact, 1-25 on the 5x5 heat map
notes.business_environment_factor_bei: capital multiplier around 1.0 from forward-looking business-environment scores
notes.internal_control_factor_icf: capital multiplier; stronger controls reduce it
notes.conduct_risk_metric: complaints/1000 + redress ratio, 0-100 index (no Basel citation)
notes.model_risk_assessment: materiality x complexity, SR 11-7 / PRA SS1/23-style tiering
notes.business_continuity_risk_score: RTO vs max tolerable downtime, BCP-maturity discounted
notes.escalation_threshold_calculation: highest governance tier a loss triggers
notes.oprisk_heat_map_generator: 5x5 likelihood x impact grid + RAG per risk
notes.audit_finding_risk_scorer: severity x likelihood + overdue-ageing uplift, capped 25
